The founder is right: backend classification must never be read off frontend presentation, and the attachment surface is generic across types, so it can evidence nothing about type resolution.

A_actualIngestionPath.path: Messages composer -> uploadAuraMedia() -> POST /media/presign -> PUT to R2 (presigned) -> POST /media/:id/confirm -> PATCH /media/:id -> message sent carrying storageKey
evidence: lib/core/attachments/aura_media_upload.dart:101 await dio.post('/media/$mediaId/confirm') — NOT wrapped in try/catch, so a 4xx propagates
A_actualIngestionPath.verdict: NO BYPASS. Every Messages attachment surface uploads through presign+confirm. The D3 storageKey door is used for the SEND, after confirm has already run over the bytes.
A_actualIngestionPath.clientErrorHandling: conversation_screen wraps the upload in try/catch, marks the attachment failed and shows 'Attachment failed — remove it and try again.' A server refusal would therefore be visible, though generically worded.

B_didTheBytesCrossContentTruth.why: confirmUpload performs a ranged read (CONTENT_TRUTH_HEAD_BYTES) and, when the head looks like a ZIP, a tail read for container inspection, then calls resolveContentTruth. media.service.ts:560-579.
B_didTheBytesCrossContentTruth.notASilentPath: On inspection failure it holds the row at UPLOADED and throws MEDIA_VERIFICATION_FAILED rather than passing the object.

C_serverDisposition.layer4: classifyZipContainer found no word/, ppt/ or xl/ member paths, so the generic ZIP was NOT refined into an OOXML type and stayed application/zip.
C_serverDisposition.persistedState: status READY, resolved mimeType application/zip, type derived from the resolved mime. The declared image/png was overridden by the bytes.
C_serverDisposition.THE_ROOT_CAUSE: application/zip IS A PERMITTED ATTACHMENT TYPE. kCanonicalAttachmentMimeMatrix carries an ARCHIVE class ['application/zip','application/x-zip-compressed'], and kDefaultPresignAllowedMimes is derived by FLATTENING EVERY CLASS. So isAllowed('application/zip') is true, and content-truth's contract is explicit: when the declared type is wrong but the actual type is permitted, CORRECT it rather than reject a legitimate upload.
C_serverDisposition.therefore: The door behaved exactly as its frozen contract specifies. Accepting the renamed ZIP is CORRECT BEHAVIOUR, not a bypass and not a defect.

D_didTheClientSuppressARefusal.answer: NO — there was no refusal to suppress.
D_didTheClientSuppressARefusal.why: The server returned success because the disposition was CORRECTED, not REJECTED. Nothing was hidden, mishandled or swallowed.
D_didTheClientSuppressARefusal.enforcementVerified: media.service.ts:595 — on REJECTED it calls failUpload(id, reason) and throws BadRequestException CONTENT_REJECTED with declared/detected details. Enforcement exists and is not advisory.

3_legVerdict.notFAIL: This contradicts both my round-1 recommendation and the founder's stated FAIL, and the reason is evidential rather than interpretive: the predeclared criterion tests what happens to a VIOLATING file. A ZIP is a PERMITTED file. The observation is accurate — the file was accepted and no refusal appeared — but it does not exercise the criterion, so it can establish neither PASS nor FAIL.
3_legVerdict.notAReinterpretation: Visible acceptance is NOT being reinterpreted as refusal. The claim is narrower: acceptance was CORRECT because the file was permitted, so the leg remains untested.
3_legVerdict.recordingAFalseFailIsAlsoHarmful: Recording FAIL against a door that behaved to specification would create a phantom defect and send repair effort at working code — the mirror of a false PASS, and equally damaging to the register.
3_legVerdict.legStatus: G1 LEG 5(B) REMAINS OPEN AND UNTESTED. G1 is not weakened.

myRepeatedError.statement: I have now twice recommended a test file that the canonical MIME policy permits — first a PDF (DOCUMENT class), then a ZIP (ARCHIVE class). Both were answered with CORRECTED, exactly as designed.
myRepeatedError.cause: I recommended from intuition about what looks like a 'violating file' instead of reading the allow-list first. The allow-list is the only thing that decides.
myRepeatedError.correctedMethod: The third case below was verified against the code BEFORE being proposed, by reading the detector's signature table and the branch that handles a missing signature.

primary.file: A plain TEXT file (any .txt with ordinary content) renamed by extension only to photo.png
primary.verifiedMechanism: The detector finds no magic-byte signature (content-truth.ts LAYER 3). The declared type image/png is NOT in UNVERIFIABLE_MIMES, which contains only text/plain and text/csv and is checked against the DECLARED type. Control therefore reaches the final branch: REJECTED, reason SIGNATURE_ABSENT_FOR_DECLARED_TYPE — 'a binary format that SHOULD have had a recognisable signature did not'.
primary.expected: Visible, truthful, recoverable refusal. The server returns 400 CONTENT_REJECTED with message 'The uploaded file could not be verified as the declared type.'

alternative.file: An SVG whose first four bytes are literally <svg, renamed to photo.png
alternative.verifiedMechanism: content-truth.ts:165 detects the <svg prefix and returns image/svg+xml, which is in kBlockedMimes and never permitted regardless of env config -> REJECTED, ACTUAL_CONTENT_NOT_PERMITTED.
alternative.caveat: It must start LITERALLY with <svg. An SVG beginning with <?xml or a BOM is not matched by the prefix rule — though such a file would still be rejected via the missing-signature branch above, for a different reason.

verifiedNextCase.whyNotAnExecutable: Not proposed: no PE/ELF signature appears in the detector's table, so an executable would reject via the missing-signature branch rather than by being identified. The text case exercises the same branch and is trivially producible.

4_5_attachmentUXGap.reason: The 451-unit baseline already contains this product gap, in TWO findings that split along the same boundary the architecture uses.

primaryOwner.canonicalText: 'Attachments in Conversation. Attachment pills render live in thread, but the send/open/download journey per attachment type ...'
primaryOwner.matchesObservation: Exactly. Pills render; the per-type open/download journey does not. This is the founder's 'can be seen but cannot be opened', the generic Attachment item, and the absence of type-appropriate actions.

secondaryOwner.canonicalText: 'Founder observed PDFs rendered as bare attachments and docx/pptx unsupported; the whole media-kind honesty model is missing.'
secondaryOwner.matchesObservation: The media-kind honesty half — the product not expressing WHAT a file is.

4_5_attachmentUXGap.theSplit: F016's ingestion half (resolving what a file actually is) is CH-11's and is working. Presenting the resolved kind with its respective actions is explicitly a CH-11 NON-GOAL owned by CH-13, and that is F011. The founder's 'legacy product gap' is F011 plus F016's presentation half.
4_5_attachmentUXGap.sharedCausationWithContentTruth: NONE ESTABLISHED. Content-truth enforcement and attachment presentation are kept as separate defects, per the founder's instruction. The only relationship is that a generic presentation surface makes backend behaviour unobservable from the UI — which is a reason not to adjudicate from screenshots, not evidence of a shared cause.
4_5_attachmentUXGap.notRedesigned: No redesign attempted. Ownership and existing evidence are now established; that was the instruction.

surfacedForAwareness.question: Should the ARCHIVE class (application/zip, application/x-zip-compressed) remain a permitted attachment type?
surfacedForAwareness.why: Archives are accepted today with ZERO examination — F137 records that no uploaded media of any kind is scanned. An archive is the classic carrier for content the door cannot see.
surfacedForAwareness.notANewFinding: This sits inside F137's existing zero-coverage scope and inside D4's phase plan. It is not a new canonical unit.
surfacedForAwareness.blocking: NOTHING. Raised because the ZIP test made it concrete, not because it gates work.
